deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily revised draft of a philosophical (epistemological) passage. It belongs to Riemann's fragment 'Antinomien' (Thesis/Antithesis: finite/infinite, discrete/continuous, etc.), printed among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' in the Gesammelte Werke (ed. Weber/Dedekind, Nachlass). The previous page's gas-law jottings (dp/p = k dρ/ρ) are unrelated to it.

The argument, stripped of deletions:
(1) The conceptual systems of the Antithesis (infinite, continuous, etc.) are sharply determined only by negative predicates (not-finite, not-discrete). They cannot be positively represented ('nicht positiv vorstellbar').
(2) Because an exact and complete representation of them is impossible, they are not open to direct investigation by our thinking.
(3) They can, however, be regarded as lying at the boundary of the representable. That is, one can form a conceptual system inside the representable which passes into the given system merely by changing its magnitude-relations ('Grössenverhältnisse').
(4) Apart from these magnitude-relations, the system stays unchanged in the passage to the limit.
(5) In the limit case itself, some of the correlative concepts lose their representability, namely those that mediate relations between other concepts.
(6) A deleted methodological version says the same thing: to understand such systems, one must first carefully develop the representable systems, then follow their relations through the passage to the limit.

In modern terms, this is a philosophical justification of the limit method: the continuum and the infinite are treated as limits of finite, discrete models whose structural relations persist and only whose magnitudes change. It parallels Riemann's practice of treating continuous manifolds and infinitesimal quantities as limits.

results.what: Epistemological principle: concepts of the 'Antithesis' (infinite, continuous) are accessible only as limit cases of representable (finite/discrete) conceptual systems obtained by changing magnitude-relations alone; in the limit, mediating relational concepts lose representability
results.modern_name: Philosophical justification of the limit/continuum method (structure preserved under passage to the limit)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann ('Antinomien' fragment, published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of Riemann's already published philosophical fragment 'Antinomien'. Its final wording matches the Werke text closely. There is no mathematics and no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: likely 'weil ein genaues und vollständiges Vorstellen' (published Werke reading), not 'angemessenes'.

The final passage should read 'Von den Grössenverhältnissen abgesehen, bleibt das Begriffssystem bei dem Uebergange zur Grenze ungeändert', not 'Wenn den Grössenverhältnissen abgesehen bleiben ... unverändert'.
Last sentence: 'In dem Grenzfalle selbst aber verlieren einige der correlativen Begriffe des Systems ihre Vorstellbarkeit', not 'die Relationsbegriffe ... einige ihre'.
'Lebergänge [?]' is a misreading: the line runs 'muss man zunächst ... vorstellbare Begriffssysteme sorgfältig ausbilden'.
The 'Uebergänge zwischen den Begriffen ... fest zu stellen' line duplicates the preceding struck/overwritten text ('Verhältnisse zwischen den Begriffen des Systems festzustellen').
'und dann seine[?] Verhältnisse' is probably 'und dann ihre Verhältnisse beim Uebergang zur Grenze verfolgen'.
The page bears folio number 30 in a circle at right margin.
